nodes.title: duplicate:layout
nodes.summary: Copies a layout whole -- objects, theme, occurrence, parts and triggers included -- or a folder and everything in it

keys.summary: the layout or folder to copy, by name; a duplicated name is `ambiguous`
the layout or folder to copy, by the id a listing or a write reported
the OUTERMOST copy's name; absent derives FileMaker's own -- "X" becomes "X Copy"
the folder to put the copy in, "/"-separated; absent leaves it beside the original
the index within the parent, 0-based as a listing emits; absent puts it right after the original
the originating add-on UUID to stamp on the COPY, which starts unowned whatever the original was

semanticChecks: `ownerId` is 32 hexadecimal digits, hyphenated or not, in either case; braces around it are refused. A read reports it back hyphen-grouped and upper case, so a caller comparing a read-back stamp against the string it sent has to fold case and drop hyphens -- the two are equal as UUIDs and different as strings.
notes: THE COPY IS COMPLETE, and that is the point of this verb rather than a claim about how thorough it is: the engine copies the catalog member's stored bytes, so everything on the layout comes across whether or not this CLI can write it. A CHART, local styling, a conditional format, a button action `create:layout` would refuse -- all of it copies. Rebuilding a layout through `create:layout` loses exactly those things, which is why copy-then-edit reaches layouts that copy-by-restatement cannot.

`newName` is OPTIONAL and absent is the useful case: the copy takes the name FileMaker Pro's own Duplicate would give it -- "Contacts" becomes "Contacts Copy", and the next copy "Contacts Copy2" -- through the engine's own generator rather than a rule restated here. There is no space before that number: it is where the engine puts it, and it is what `update:layout`'s `duplicateObjects` names a copied OBJECT too.

SO A COPY USUALLY DOES NOT SHARE THE ORIGINAL'S NAME, but `newName` may be set to anything, the original's name included: duplicate names are legal (see the catalog's own note) and are not refused here either. The result reports the copy's `id`, which is the address that works either way.

Absent `folder` and `position`, the copy lands IMMEDIATELY AFTER the original, which is what FileMaker Pro's Manage Layouts does. `folder` alone appends to that folder; `position` alone indexes within the ORIGINAL's own folder. `folder`:"" is the top level.

A FOLDER COPIES WITH EVERYTHING IN IT -- nested folders, separators and all, in the order they were in, each nested folder closed with a bracket of its own. There is no `recursive` flag and no reason for one: copying adds rather than destroys, and a folder copied without its contents is an empty folder, which `create:layout` already makes. The copy lands after the original's CLOSING bracket, so "beside it" never means "inside it".

ONLY THE OUTERMOST COPY IS RENAMED. The layouts inside a copied folder keep the names they had, which is FileMaker Pro's rule as well: a folder whose every layout came out as "X Copy" is a rename nobody asked for, and the folder's own new name already says which copy it is.

A SEPARATOR IS A LAYOUT NAMED "-", and it is the one name the derivation leaves alone: "- Copy" would be an ordinary entry in the Layouts menu rather than a second divider, so the copy keeps the name. FileMaker Pro suppresses the suffix on exactly this name. An explicit `newName` still renames it.

`objectsDuplicated` is every object the copy carries, at every depth, summed over every layout copied, and `membersDuplicated` is how many CATALOG MEMBERS were created -- 1 for a layout, and for a folder both of its brackets plus everything between. `createdObjectIds` is NOT reported: a copied store keeps the original's object ids, since ids are scoped to the layout they are on, so a list of them would be the original's numbers under a name meaning new ones. Read the copy back by its `id` to address its objects.

OBJECT UUIDs COME ACROSS UNCHANGED, matching FileMaker Pro's own Duplicate Layout. They identify an object within its own layout, so the copy's are unique where it matters; only `update:layout`'s `duplicateObjects`, which copies inside ONE layout, has to mint new ones.

The copy is UNOWNED whatever the original was -- the engine clears the add-on stamp as part of copying, and demotes an add-on's primary mark on the member to a possible-secondary one. `ownerId` stamps the copy; it does not override anything, and it stamps every member of a copied folder so that a folder is never half-owned.

The objects INSIDE the copy keep whatever add-on stamps they carried, unlike the member's own. That is the engine's position rather than this CLI's: the demoted member mark is how FileMaker records "this may be a copy of an add-on's layout", and erasing the stamps underneath it would throw away the association that mark exists to keep.

A COPY OF A THEMELESS LAYOUT GETS THE FILE'S DEFAULT THEME, with a warning naming the layout, rather than copying the broken state -- the same repair `update:layout` makes, for the same reason. The original is left exactly as it was.

Nothing that referred to the ORIGINAL refers to the copy. A script's `Go to Layout` step, a button, a portal -- each names one layout, and this CLI does not rewrite them, so a copy made to replace a layout has to be pointed at by hand.
seeAlso: `fm-cli help forms` — what JSON a key's type, its requiredness and a filter's tag each take

nodes.title: read:layout
nodes.summary: Lists the Layouts menu as a tree, or describes one layout, with the objects on it on request
semanticChecks: a filter needs 'flatten':true. A listing is nested by default, so a filter could only test the top level and would silently drop every match inside a folder.
notes: A listing is a TREE by default and its `total` counts nodes at every depth, not top-level members. A folder carries `items`; a layout never does.

`flatten` returns the SAME members as one flat array instead of a tree, each carrying the `folder` path it sits in -- absolute, "/"-separated, and "" at the top level, so it feeds straight back into create:layout's or update:layout's own `folder`. Folders are still reported (an empty one would otherwise be invisible) but carry no `items`, so `type` is the discriminator in every mode. Order is depth-first: a folder, then its contents, which is the Layouts menu read top to bottom.

`position` is PARENT-relative in both modes and is never renumbered across a flattened list, so the same member reports the same number either way and `folder` plus `position` stays the address an ordering write targets.

`filter` narrows a listing to the members matching every attribute given, and needs `flatten`:true. A nested listing is a tree, so a filter over it could only test the top level and would drop matches sitting inside folders; flattening puts every member in reach. `total` still counts every member the listing covers and `returned` counts what matched, so a filter that matches nothing is an empty `items` rather than an error. Filtering by `tableOccurrence` never returns a folder, which has none.

`folder` scopes a listing to one folder's subtree and composes with `flatten`, which is the pairing to reach for: it answers "every member inside this folder, however deep". `total` then counts that subtree rather than the file. A path component matching two folders at one level is `ambiguous` with the candidate ids rather than a guess at which subtree was meant.

A DESCRIBE CARRIES NO SUBTREE, folders included. A folder describe answers what the folder IS -- its id, position and `hidden` -- and `read:layout` with `folder` is the one way to ask what is inside it. A describe does report its own `folder`, so a caller can always learn where a layout lives.

AN EMPTY TREE IS AN ORDINARY ANSWER for a file that came from elsewhere, though no file `--create` makes is empty: it is given one layout, named after the file. Creating a table adds no layout -- FileMaker Pro's UI mints one for a new table, this CLI does not.

Layout names are NOT unique, so a describe by a name two members share is `ambiguous` listing the candidate ids rather than a first match, which would make read:layout non-deterministic across files differing only in creation order.

A describe reports what is STORED. Access levels are deliberately absent: access is a property of the reader rather than of the layout, and it measured read-write on all 25 layouts of three real files.

`detail` reports EVERY object type, as a tree, which is not the Data API's two flat lists -- because update:layout can add and remove objects and a caller deciding whether that is safe has to see what else is there. `unmodelledCount` is how many objects an update would leave untouched.

A WEB VIEWER reports `type`:"webViewer" with a `webViewer` object carrying its `urlCalculation` and its six settings, and `urlCalculation` is what `update:layout` accepts back. A CHART reports `type`:"chart" and nothing more -- the two are the same FileMaker object type internally, told apart by an id the object carries, and only one of them has a definition this CLI can read.

A BUTTON reports `type`:"button" with the text on its face as `text` -- the same key a label uses, because it is the same thing stored the same way, and it is what `update:layout` accepts back. No `text` means an unlabelled button, which is ordinary.

A BUTTON ALWAYS REPORTS `action`, which is WHAT IT DOES, and it is THE SAME STEP OBJECT ONE LINE OF A SCRIPT'S `body` IS. `stepID` is the discriminator, `step` is the step's name, and the rest of the keys are that step's own -- a Perform Script button reports `{"stepID":1,"step":"Perform Script","script":"Invoice"}`, exactly as a Perform Script line inside a script does. So `read:script` and a button's `action` are read the same way, and what you learn about one applies to the other.

EVERY STEP IS REPORTED: a button carrying Send Mail reports a Send Mail step with its real settings. `create:layout` and `update:layout` TAKE THE SAME OBJECT BACK under their own `action` key, so a read followed by a write is a round trip and not a translation. Sixteen step ids are read here and refused on the way in, because FileMaker itself will not put them on a button. A button's step is not editable through `update:script`, which reads and writes scripts rather than buttons.

A BUTTON THAT DOES NOTHING reports `{"stepID":0}`. Step 0 is not a step: it is what FileMaker stores for a button whose setup dialog was never answered, and "Do Nothing" is one of the choices in that dialog. The key is present on every button rather than omitted for this case, because a missing key would leave "this button does nothing" and "this build does not say" spelled the same, and the second reading is the one that gets a live button treated as decoration.

A POPOVER IS REPORTED AT THE TOP LEVEL, NOT INSIDE THE BUTTON THAT OPENS IT, and that is the layout's real shape rather than an omission here. FileMaker stores a popover button and its popover as two SEPARATE objects that point at each other, and it keeps the popover in the layout's own object list wherever the button happens to sit -- so a button inside a tab panel still has its popover at the top level. FileMaker Pro's own interface draws the popover under its button and hides this. Reading `contents` top-down, expect an object of `type`:"popover" with no enclosing button, and expect the `type`:"popoverButton" that opens it to be somewhere else entirely; the objects INSIDE the popover are reported as its children, where they are stored.

A web viewer also reports `border`, and only the sides the OBJECT states -- a side that is absent is one its theme decides, which is not the same as "none" because every FileMaker theme draws a line around a web viewer. One created by this CLI reports all four sides "none". No other object kind reports a border.

A GRAPHIC reports `pictureId`, which says WHICH PICTURE it shows and nothing else -- not the size, not the format, and not where the picture came from, because the file stores the picture rather than its origin. Two graphics report the SAME number exactly when they show the same picture: FileMaker keeps one copy of each distinct picture in the file's image library and keys it by the bytes, so a duplicated graphic and a second `create:layout` from a byte-identical file both land on the number the first one has. It is not a write address -- give `picture` a file, and identical bytes reach the member the file already holds. Absent for a graphic holding no embedded picture, which is what an OLE object or a stored file reference is.

`geometry.bodyHeight` is the body part's height alongside `geometry.baseWidth`, and both write verbs take them under those same two names, so a describe round-trips into a write. Absent for a layout with no body part, which this CLI never creates but FileMaker Pro can (a header/footer-only report layout, for instance).

Every object in `contents` carries an `id` -- the object's own persistent key, which is what names one object when `name` is absent (most objects carry none) or shared. It is SCOPED TO THE LAYOUT, not to the file, unlike every other `id` here: two layouts of one file both hold an object 1. It survives a commit and a reopen, and a deleted object's number is not reused, so ids read once stay valid in later invocations. It is also a WRITE address: `update:layout`'s `removeObjects` takes `{"id":N}`.

Every object in `contents` carries `anchors` -- FileMaker's Inspector "Position" tab, as four booleans -- for every one of the nineteen types, not just the ones this CLI can write. All four true is what fills the window as it resizes; top+left only (the default for an untouched object) fixes it in place. A PANEL AND A SEGMENT REPORT THEIR PARENT'S FOUR rather than their own, which is what Pro shows for them: a panel is forced to its control's rectangle, so it has no independent size for an anchor to act on.

EVERY OBJECT ALSO CARRIES THE SIX SETTINGS of Pro's padlock and its Sliding & Visibility section: `locked`, `hideWhenPrinting`, `slideLeft`, `slideUp`, `slideBasedOn` (`allAbove` or `directlyAbove`) and `resizeEnclosingPart`. All six on all nineteen types, always -- each is one setting of the word every object carries, so there is no absent state. They read the way Pro's controls do, `hideWhenPrinting` included: true means the object is left out of a print. A PANEL AND A SEGMENT REPORT THEIR PARENT'S SIX, the same as `anchors`, so a tab control and its panels always agree on them. `slideBasedOn` is FileMaker's two radio buttons under "Sliding up based on:" and applies when `slideUp` is on.

A CONTROL AND A BAR SAY WHICH OF THEIR CHILDREN THEY SINGLE OUT, and nothing else in the output implies it. A tab or slide control carries `visiblePanel`, the `id` of the panel it opens on, and a tab control also carries `defaultPanel` -- Pro's "Default Front Tab". They are NOT the first entry of `objects`: a control's panels can be reordered without changing which one opens, so a control with three panels can report the second. A button bar carries `activeSegment` when a segment is marked as the current one, which FileMaker leaves unset on an ordinary bar. Each is absent when the object singles nothing out, and a slide control carries no `defaultPanel` because FileMaker stores none for one -- its default is its first panel, which `objects` already says.

An object carrying a NAMED THEME STYLE reports it under `style`, as the display name Pro's Inspector shows in its Style pop-up. Absent means the object wears its theme's default for its kind, which most objects do. The name is the theme's, not the object's: what the object stores is an internal id (`primary_button`, or `FM-38B338BC-...` for a style a developer made), and the theme holds the mapping. `update:layout`'s `style` takes the display name back, and "" removes the binding. ONE NAME CAN BE SEVERAL STYLES -- 'Transparent' is a different style for a button than for an edit box -- so the object's kind is what decides which one a write applies, and a name defined only for other kinds is refused with the list of what this object can wear.

A TURNED OBJECT reports `rotation` in whole degrees -- 90, 180 or 270. Absent means the object is upright, which is nearly all of them. IT DOES NOT AFFECT `bounds`: the rectangle reported is the stored one whatever the angle is, so a turned field reports the same rectangle it would have reported before it was turned. The file holds tenths of a degree internally, which is what a DDR export shows as 2700; the wire never uses them.

A POPOVER reports `popoverArrow`, which of its OWN edges carries the arrow pointing at its button -- so the popover opens on the OPPOSITE side: a popover reporting `left` sits to the RIGHT of its button. FileMaker's own vocabulary and its DDR export use the same words. It says which edge FileMaker will TRY FIRST when the popover opens, not where the popover will appear: the fallback goes through the other edges when the first does not fit the screen, and in Layout mode the popover keeps whatever rectangle `bounds` reports.

A POPOVER also reports `showTitleBar`, always, and it reads the way Pro's checkbox does: false means the strip along the top of the popover is not drawn. The file stores the opposite bit, `kHideTitleBar`, so a DDR export's raw flag number is the negation of this. A popover whose bar is hidden STILL REPORTS ITS `title`, because the title is stored separately and comes back when the bar does.

A BUTTON BAR reports `orientation`, `horizontal` or `vertical`, always and on nothing else. A SEGMENT does not report it: which way the bar runs is what decides where each segment sits, so it belongs to the bar a segment is nested under. `update:layout` takes the word back and turning the bar moves every segment while leaving the bar's own `bounds` alone.

A GROUP reports `action`, the same step object a button does and always, because FileMaker turns a group into a button by giving it a script step -- that is what Pro's Button Setup dialog does to a selection. A group with no action reports `{"stepID": 0}`, FileMaker's own "Do Nothing", and is an ordinary group rather than a broken button.

A SLIDE CONTROL reports `showNavigationDots` and `enableSwipeGestures`, which are the two checkboxes in Pro's Slide Control Setup dialog. Both are always reported on a slide control and on nothing else. THEY READ THE WAY PRO'S CHECKBOXES DO: `showNavigationDots` false means the dots are hidden. The file stores the opposite two bits, so a DDR export's raw `slideFlagSet` number is the negation of these; `update:layout` takes the same two words back in the same sense. Neither affects the control's panels or its rectangle -- hiding the dots does not reclaim the space they occupied, which is the style's to give.

A TAB CONTROL reports `tabWidthStyle`, `tabWidthModifier`, `tabWidthUnits` and `tabsShareSingleStyle` -- the stored parts of Pro's Tab Control Setup dialog, on the control and not on its panels. `tabWidthModifier` IS IN POINTS whatever `tabWidthUnits` says; the unit is only what Pro's dialog displays, and it is the one of the four that can be absent, because the stored field can hold a value naming no unit. The modifier is used by three of the five width styles and is reported for all of them. THE TAB POSITION AND THE TAB HEIGHT ARE NOT REPORTED, deliberately: nothing in FileMaker reads the position and the height is recomputed from the font on every layout pass, so neither is a setting a caller could act on.

A FIELD reports Pro's Inspector Behavior section: `browseEntry` and `findEntry`, then `selectContentsOnEntry`, `exitOnTab`, `exitOnReturn`, `exitOnEnter`, `applyVisualSpellChecking`, `quickFind`, `inputMode` and `keyboardType`. The first eight are always present on a field; `inputMode` and `keyboardType` are absent only when the stored byte holds a value naming none of their options, which FileMaker itself cannot author. THE ENTRY VALUES ARE PRO'S PICKER WORDS -- `edit`, `selectOnly`, `viewOnly` and `setByCalculation` -- and a field reading `setByCalculation` is entered or not according to its `entryCalculation`, which is reported beside them. `applyVisualSpellChecking` and `quickFind` READ POSITIVELY: true means misspellings are underlined and the field is searched, which is the opposite sense from the bits the file stores. A LABEL REPORTS `quickFind` TOO, and only where FileMaker would offer it: a label's Quick Find searches the FIELDS its merge fields reference, so the key appears on a label carrying at least one merge field that names a searchable field and is absent on every other label. Absent rather than false, because the engine ignores the stored value on a label it will not search, so a reported false would be a value the write then refuses.

A FIELD also reports the rest of Pro's Data section, always: `repetitionCount` and `repetitionOrientation`, `allowEntryOfOtherValues`, `allowEditingOfValueList`, `includeShowHideIcon`, `autoComplete`, `showVerticalScrollBar`, `scrollBarVisibility`, `showPlaceholderInFindMode` and `overrideDataFormattingWithValueList` -- alongside `control` and `valueList`, which are that section's first two controls. EVERY ONE IS REPORTED WHATEVER THE CONTROL STYLE, because the file stores each either way and a caller reproducing a field needs all of them; `allowEditingOfValueList` on an edit box is stored and inert rather than absent. `repetitionCount` IS THE COUNT WITHOUT ITS SIGN -- the file keeps one signed number whose sign is the orientation, and reporting it raw would hide a layout choice inside a quantity. `includeShowHideIcon` is the checkbox a developer ticks; whether a pop-up menu actually draws the icon also depends on a compatibility bit this CLI sets for you when you write the key.

A FIELD AND A GRAPHIC BOTH REPORT how the picture inside them is fitted, which is the Graphic tab of Pro's Data Formatting section: `graphicSizing` (`cropToFrame`, `reduceToFit`, `enlargeToFit` or `reduceOrEnlargeToFit`), `maintainOriginalProportions`, `horizontalAlignment` (`left`, `center` or `right`) and `verticalAlignment` (`top`, `center` or `bottom`). All four always, on both kinds. WHAT MADE THE OBJECT SHOWS UP HERE: a field this CLI created reports `cropToFrame` with proportions false, one FileMaker Pro created reports `reduceToFit` with proportions TRUE, and a GRAPHIC this CLI created reports `reduceOrEnlargeToFit` with proportions FALSE -- so its picture is stretched to fill the object until you set `maintainOriginalProportions`. An alignment is ABSENT only for a stored value naming no choice, which FileMaker's own pickers cannot produce.

A FIELD ALSO REPORTS THE FOUR SETTINGS FOR INTERACTIVE CONTENT, and a graphic does not: `optimizeFor` (`images` or `interactiveContent`), `autoPlay`, `noContextMenu` and `preservePdfTransparency`. They are the rest of the same Graphic tab and they are what makes a container field show a PDF, an audio file or a video rather than a still picture. A GRAPHIC REPORTS NONE OF THEM even though it has somewhere to keep them, because nothing in FileMaker reads them on one -- a graphic's transparency is preserved regardless of what is stored. So a write for these four is refused on a graphic, and reporting them there would put four values in front of you that writing the object back would be refused for. `noContextMenu` READS AS IT SOUNDS: true means the shortcut menu over a PDF is suppressed.

EVERY KIND REPORTS ITS CALCULATION-BACKED SETTINGS, and each of them carries the EXPRESSION the way FileMaker's calculation dialog shows it: `tooltip`, `hideCondition`, `accessibilityTitle` and `accessibilityHelp`, plus `placeholderText` and `entryCalculation` on a FIELD. A value a developer typed as plain text reads back QUOTED -- `"Hello there"` -- because that is what the file holds; a formula reads back unquoted. Each is ABSENT unless the object has one. `applyInFindMode` is the checkbox beside the hide condition and is reported ALWAYS on every kind, so it can be true with no `hideCondition` beside it -- which is a state FileMaker leaves behind when a condition is cleared in Pro, and it hides nothing. A TAB OR SLIDE PANEL REPORTS ITS CONTROL's `hideCondition` and `applyInFindMode`, because that is where FileMaker keeps them for a panel; the tooltip and the two accessibility strings are the panel's own.

`accessibilityLabel` IS ANOTHER OBJECT'S `id` -- the object whose text labels this one for a screen reader, which is Pro's "Click to select..." button in the Accessibility section. It is ABSENT both when the object has no label and when the stored reference names an object that is no longer on the layout, because reporting that would give you an `id` nothing resolves. Send 0 to clear one.

`scriptTriggers` ON AN OBJECT IS THAT OBJECT'S OWN, one entry per event, and it is a different set of events from the layout's `scriptTriggers` above -- OnObjectEnter, OnObjectExit, OnObjectModify, OnObjectSave, OnObjectKeystroke, OnObjectValidate, OnObjectAVPlayerChange, and OnPanelSwitch on a tab or slide control. Each entry names the `event`, the `script` it runs, the `modes` it fires in and its `parameter` if it has one, exactly as a layout trigger's does. THE KEY IS ABSENT ON A KIND THAT CANNOT HOLD A TRIGGER and `[]` on one that can and does not -- a label, a shape, a graphic, a button bar, a tab or slide PANEL and a group with no action report no key at all, and that is the same distinction `objects` draws between an empty container and a leaf. So the key appears exactly where a write for it is accepted, with one exception: a CHART reports its triggers and refuses every write, because this CLI cannot change a chart at all.

A BUTTON AND A POPOVER BUTTON REPORT THEIR ICON as `iconId`, `iconSize` and `iconPosition`, and a button bar SEGMENT reports them too -- a segment is a button. `iconId` is the image-library member the icon is stored as, the same kind of number `pictureId` is and in the same catalog, and it is ABSENT on a button with no icon. It is an identity rather than a write address: `icon` takes a FILE, and a file the library already holds is joined rather than stored twice. The other two are reported whatever the icon is, because the file stores them either way -- so `iconSize` on a button with no icon is the size an icon WOULD be drawn at, which is why a Pro-authored button with nothing showing still reports 16. AN ICON DRIVEN BY A CALCULATION IS NOT VISIBLE HERE: these three read normally on such a button, so what is reported can be an icon a formula overrides when it is drawn.

`showHandCursor` IS REPORTED WHEREVER FILEMAKER READS IT and absent everywhere else, so it appears exactly where a write for it is taken: on a BUTTON, a POPOVER BUTTON, a button bar SEGMENT, and on a GROUP once it carries an `action`. A group with no action reports no key, which is the same absent-versus-present distinction `scriptTriggers` draws and for the same reason -- a script step is what makes a group a button.

A PORTAL reports five of Pro's Portal Setup settings, always, and on nothing else: `initialRow`, `allowVerticalScrolling`, `scrollBarVisibility`, `allowDelete` and `resetScrollBarOnExit`. Each reads the way the dialog does, so `resetScrollBarOnExit` true means the scroll position is NOT retained -- the file stores the retaining bit and this is its negation. WATCH WHICH KEY IS WHICH CONTROL: `allowVerticalScrolling` is the checkbox and `scrollBarVisibility` (`always` or `whenScrolling`) is the picker beside it, which is the one the dialog labels "Show scroll bar:". The picker is reported even on a portal with no bar, where Pro greys it out, because the file stores it either way. `initialRow` is 1-BASED -- which row of the found set the portal starts at. THE DIALOG HOLDS MORE THAN THESE FIVE: its sort and its filter are backed by a stored sort order and a calculation and are reported nowhere yet, and its two row-styling checkboxes are styling. So these five do not describe a portal completely.

notes: A listing is a TREE by default and its `total` counts nodes at every depth, not top-level members. A folder carries `items`; a layout never does.

`flatten` returns the SAME members as one flat array instead of a tree, each carrying the `folder` path it sits in -- absolute, "/"-separated, and "" at the top level, so it feeds straight back into create:layout's or update:layout's own `folder`. Folders are still reported (an empty one would otherwise be invisible) but carry no `items`, so `type` is the discriminator in every mode. Order is depth-first: a folder, then its contents, which is the Layouts menu read top to bottom.

`position` is PARENT-relative in both modes and is never renumbered across a flattened list, so the same member reports the same number either way and `folder` plus `position` stays the address an ordering write targets.

`filter` narrows a listing to the members matching every attribute given, and needs `flatten`:true. A nested listing is a tree, so a filter over it could only test the top level and would drop matches sitting inside folders; flattening puts every member in reach. `total` still counts every member the listing covers and `returned` counts what matched, so a filter that matches nothing is an empty `items` rather than an error. Filtering by `tableOccurrence` never returns a folder, which has none.

`folder` scopes a listing to one folder's subtree and composes with `flatten`, which is the pairing to reach for: it answers "every member inside this folder, however deep". `total` then counts that subtree rather than the file. A path component matching two folders at one level is `ambiguous` with the candidate ids rather than a guess at which subtree was meant.

A DESCRIBE CARRIES NO SUBTREE, folders included. A folder describe answers what the folder IS -- its id, position and `hidden` -- and `read:layout` with `folder` is the one way to ask what is inside it. A describe does report its own `folder`, so a caller can always learn where a layout lives.

AN EMPTY TREE IS AN ORDINARY ANSWER for a file that came from elsewhere, though no file `--create` makes is empty: it is given one layout, named after the file. Creating a table adds no layout -- FileMaker Pro's UI mints one for a new table, this CLI does not.

Layout names are NOT unique, so a describe by a name two members share is `ambiguous` listing the candidate ids rather than a first match, which would make read:layout non-deterministic across files differing only in creation order.

A describe reports what is STORED. Access levels are deliberately absent: access is a property of the reader rather than of the layout, and it measured read-write on all 25 layouts of three real files.

`detail` reports EVERY object type, as a tree, which is not the Data API's two flat lists -- because update:layout can add and remove objects and a caller deciding whether that is safe has to see what else is there. `unmodelledCount` is how many objects an update would leave untouched.

A WEB VIEWER reports `type`:"webViewer" with a `webViewer` object carrying its `urlCalculation` and its six settings, and `urlCalculation` is what `update:layout` accepts back. A CHART reports `type`:"chart" and nothing more -- the two are the same FileMaker object type internally, told apart by an id the object carries, and only one of them has a definition this CLI can read.

A BUTTON reports `type`:"button" with the text on its face as `text` -- the same key a label uses, because it is the same thing stored the same way, and it is what `update:layout` accepts back. No `text` means an unlabelled button, which is ordinary.

A BUTTON ALWAYS REPORTS `action`, which is WHAT IT DOES, and it is THE SAME STEP OBJECT ONE LINE OF A SCRIPT'S `body` IS. `stepID` is the discriminator, `step` is the step's name, and the rest of the keys are that step's own -- a Perform Script button reports `{"stepID":1,"step":"Perform Script","script":"Invoice"}`, exactly as a Perform Script line inside a script does. So `read:script` and a button's `action` are read the same way, and what you learn about one applies to the other.

EVERY STEP IS REPORTED: a button carrying Send Mail reports a Send Mail step with its real settings. `create:layout` and `update:layout` TAKE THE SAME OBJECT BACK under their own `action` key, so a read followed by a write is a round trip and not a translation. Sixteen step ids are read here and refused on the way in, because FileMaker itself will not put them on a button. A button's step is not editable through `update:script`, which reads and writes scripts rather than buttons.

A BUTTON THAT DOES NOTHING reports `{"stepID":0}`. Step 0 is not a step: it is what FileMaker stores for a button whose setup dialog was never answered, and "Do Nothing" is one of the choices in that dialog. The key is present on every button rather than omitted for this case, because a missing key would leave "this button does nothing" and "this build does not say" spelled the same, and the second reading is the one that gets a live button treated as decoration.

A POPOVER IS REPORTED AT THE TOP LEVEL, NOT INSIDE THE BUTTON THAT OPENS IT, and that is the layout's real shape rather than an omission here. FileMaker stores a popover button and its popover as two SEPARATE objects that point at each other, and it keeps the popover in the layout's own object list wherever the button happens to sit -- so a button inside a tab panel still has its popover at the top level. FileMaker Pro's own interface draws the popover under its button and hides this. Reading `contents` top-down, expect an object of `type`:"popover" with no enclosing button, and expect the `type`:"popoverButton" that opens it to be somewhere else entirely; the objects INSIDE the popover are reported as its children, where they are stored.

A web viewer also reports `border`, and only the sides the OBJECT states -- a side that is absent is one its theme decides, which is not the same as "none" because every FileMaker theme draws a line around a web viewer. One created by this CLI reports all four sides "none". No other object kind reports a border.

A GRAPHIC reports `pictureId`, which says WHICH PICTURE it shows and nothing else -- not the size, not the format, and not where the picture came from, because the file stores the picture rather than its origin. Two graphics report the SAME number exactly when they show the same picture: FileMaker keeps one copy of each distinct picture in the file's image library and keys it by the bytes, so a duplicated graphic and a second `create:layout` from a byte-identical file both land on the number the first one has. It is not a write address -- give `picture` a file, and identical bytes reach the member the file already holds. Absent for a graphic holding no embedded picture, which is what an OLE object or a stored file reference is.

`geometry.bodyHeight` is the body part's height alongside `geometry.baseWidth`, and both write verbs take them under those same two names, so a describe round-trips into a write. Absent for a layout with no body part, which this CLI never creates but FileMaker Pro can (a header/footer-only report layout, for instance).

Every object in `contents` carries an `id` -- the object's own persistent key, which is what names one object when `name` is absent (most objects carry none) or shared. It is SCOPED TO THE LAYOUT, not to the file, unlike every other `id` here: two layouts of one file both hold an object 1. It survives a commit and a reopen, and a deleted object's number is not reused, so ids read once stay valid in later invocations. It is also a WRITE address: `update:layout`'s `removeObjects` takes `{"id":N}`.

Every object in `contents` carries `anchors` -- FileMaker's Inspector "Position" tab, as four booleans -- for every one of the nineteen types, not just the ones this CLI can write. All four true is what fills the window as it resizes; top+left only (the default for an untouched object) fixes it in place. A PANEL AND A SEGMENT REPORT THEIR PARENT'S FOUR rather than their own, which is what Pro shows for them: a panel is forced to its control's rectangle, so it has no independent size for an anchor to act on.

EVERY OBJECT ALSO CARRIES THE SIX SETTINGS of Pro's padlock and its Sliding & Visibility section: `locked`, `hideWhenPrinting`, `slideLeft`, `slideUp`, `slideBasedOn` (`allAbove` or `directlyAbove`) and `resizeEnclosingPart`. All six on all nineteen types, always -- each is one setting of the word every object carries, so there is no absent state. They read the way Pro's controls do, `hideWhenPrinting` included: true means the object is left out of a print. A PANEL AND A SEGMENT REPORT THEIR PARENT'S SIX, the same as `anchors`, so a tab control and its panels always agree on them. `slideBasedOn` is FileMaker's two radio buttons under "Sliding up based on:" and applies when `slideUp` is on.

A CONTROL AND A BAR SAY WHICH OF THEIR CHILDREN THEY SINGLE OUT, and nothing else in the output implies it. A tab or slide control carries `visiblePanel`, the `id` of the panel it opens on, and a tab control also carries `defaultPanel` -- Pro's "Default Front Tab". They are NOT the first entry of `objects`: a control's panels can be reordered without changing which one opens, so a control with three panels can report the second. A button bar carries `activeSegment` when a segment is marked as the current one, which FileMaker leaves unset on an ordinary bar. Each is absent when the object singles nothing out, and a slide control carries no `defaultPanel` because FileMaker stores none for one -- its default is its first panel, which `objects` already says.

An object carrying a NAMED THEME STYLE reports it under `style`, as the display name Pro's Inspector shows in its Style pop-up. Absent means the object wears its theme's default for its kind, which most objects do. The name is the theme's, not the object's: what the object stores is an internal id (`primary_button`, or `FM-38B338BC-...` for a style a developer made), and the theme holds the mapping. `update:layout`'s `style` takes the display name back, and "" removes the binding. ONE NAME CAN BE SEVERAL STYLES -- 'Transparent' is a different style for a button than for an edit box -- so the object's kind is what decides which one a write applies, and a name defined only for other kinds is refused with the list of what this object can wear.

A TURNED OBJECT reports `rotation` in whole degrees -- 90, 180 or 270. Absent means the object is upright, which is nearly all of them. IT DOES NOT AFFECT `bounds`: the rectangle reported is the stored one whatever the angle is, so a turned field reports the same rectangle it would have reported before it was turned. The file holds tenths of a degree internally, which is what a DDR export shows as 2700; the wire never uses them.

A POPOVER reports `popoverArrow`, which of its OWN edges carries the arrow pointing at its button -- so the popover opens on the OPPOSITE side: a popover reporting `left` sits to the RIGHT of its button. FileMaker's own vocabulary and its DDR export use the same words. It says which edge FileMaker will TRY FIRST when the popover opens, not where the popover will appear: the fallback goes through the other edges when the first does not fit the screen, and in Layout mode the popover keeps whatever rectangle `bounds` reports.

A POPOVER also reports `showTitleBar`, always, and it reads the way Pro's checkbox does: false means the strip along the top of the popover is not drawn. The file stores the opposite bit, `kHideTitleBar`, so a DDR export's raw flag number is the negation of this. A popover whose bar is hidden STILL REPORTS ITS `title`, because the title is stored separately and comes back when the bar does.

A BUTTON BAR reports `orientation`, `horizontal` or `vertical`, always and on nothing else. A SEGMENT does not report it: which way the bar runs is what decides where each segment sits, so it belongs to the bar a segment is nested under. `update:layout` takes the word back and turning the bar moves every segment while leaving the bar's own `bounds` alone.

A GROUP reports `action`, the same step object a button does and always, because FileMaker turns a group into a button by giving it a script step -- that is what Pro's Button Setup dialog does to a selection. A group with no action reports `{"stepID": 0}`, FileMaker's own "Do Nothing", and is an ordinary group rather than a broken button.

A SLIDE CONTROL reports `showNavigationDots` and `enableSwipeGestures`, which are the two checkboxes in Pro's Slide Control Setup dialog. Both are always reported on a slide control and on nothing else. THEY READ THE WAY PRO'S CHECKBOXES DO: `showNavigationDots` false means the dots are hidden. The file stores the opposite two bits, so a DDR export's raw `slideFlagSet` number is the negation of these; `update:layout` takes the same two words back in the same sense. Neither affects the control's panels or its rectangle -- hiding the dots does not reclaim the space they occupied, which is the style's to give.

A TAB CONTROL reports `tabWidthStyle`, `tabWidthModifier`, `tabWidthUnits` and `tabsShareSingleStyle` -- the stored parts of Pro's Tab Control Setup dialog, on the control and not on its panels. `tabWidthModifier` IS IN POINTS whatever `tabWidthUnits` says; the unit is only what Pro's dialog displays, and it is the one of the four that can be absent, because the stored field can hold a value naming no unit. The modifier is used by three of the five width styles and is reported for all of them. THE TAB POSITION AND THE TAB HEIGHT ARE NOT REPORTED, deliberately: nothing in FileMaker reads the position and the height is recomputed from the font on every layout pass, so neither is a setting a caller could act on.

A FIELD reports Pro's Inspector Behavior section: `browseEntry` and `findEntry`, then `selectContentsOnEntry`, `exitOnTab`, `exitOnReturn`, `exitOnEnter`, `applyVisualSpellChecking`, `quickFind`, `inputMode` and `keyboardType`. The first eight are always present on a field; `inputMode` and `keyboardType` are absent only when the stored byte holds a value naming none of their options, which FileMaker itself cannot author. THE ENTRY VALUES ARE PRO'S PICKER WORDS -- `edit`, `selectOnly`, `viewOnly` and `setByCalculation` -- and a field reading `setByCalculation` is entered or not according to its `entryCalculation`, which is reported beside them. `applyVisualSpellChecking` and `quickFind` READ POSITIVELY: true means misspellings are underlined and the field is searched, which is the opposite sense from the bits the file stores. A LABEL REPORTS `quickFind` TOO, and only where FileMaker would offer it: a label's Quick Find searches the FIELDS its merge fields reference, so the key appears on a label carrying at least one merge field that names a searchable field and is absent on every other label. Absent rather than false, because the engine ignores the stored value on a label it will not search, so a reported false would be a value the write then refuses.

A FIELD also reports the rest of Pro's Data section, always: `repetitionCount` and `repetitionOrientation`, `allowEntryOfOtherValues`, `allowEditingOfValueList`, `includeShowHideIcon`, `autoComplete`, `showVerticalScrollBar`, `scrollBarVisibility`, `showPlaceholderInFindMode` and `overrideDataFormattingWithValueList` -- alongside `control` and `valueList`, which are that section's first two controls. EVERY ONE IS REPORTED WHATEVER THE CONTROL STYLE, because the file stores each either way and a caller reproducing a field needs all of them; `allowEditingOfValueList` on an edit box is stored and inert rather than absent. `repetitionCount` IS THE COUNT WITHOUT ITS SIGN -- the file keeps one signed number whose sign is the orientation, and reporting it raw would hide a layout choice inside a quantity. `includeShowHideIcon` is the checkbox a developer ticks; whether a pop-up menu actually draws the icon also depends on a compatibility bit this CLI sets for you when you write the key.

A FIELD AND A GRAPHIC BOTH REPORT how the picture inside them is fitted, which is the Graphic tab of Pro's Data Formatting section: `graphicSizing` (`cropToFrame`, `reduceToFit`, `enlargeToFit` or `reduceOrEnlargeToFit`), `maintainOriginalProportions`, `horizontalAlignment` (`left`, `center` or `right`) and `verticalAlignment` (`top`, `center` or `bottom`). All four always, on both kinds. WHAT MADE THE OBJECT SHOWS UP HERE: a field this CLI created reports `cropToFrame` with proportions false, one FileMaker Pro created reports `reduceToFit` with proportions TRUE, and a GRAPHIC this CLI created reports `reduceOrEnlargeToFit` with proportions FALSE -- so its picture is stretched to fill the object until you set `maintainOriginalProportions`. An alignment is ABSENT only for a stored value naming no choice, which FileMaker's own pickers cannot produce.

A FIELD ALSO REPORTS THE FOUR SETTINGS FOR INTERACTIVE CONTENT, and a graphic does not: `optimizeFor` (`images` or `interactiveContent`), `autoPlay`, `noContextMenu` and `preservePdfTransparency`. They are the rest of the same Graphic tab and they are what makes a container field show a PDF, an audio file or a video rather than a still picture. A GRAPHIC REPORTS NONE OF THEM even though it has somewhere to keep them, because nothing in FileMaker reads them on one -- a graphic's transparency is preserved regardless of what is stored. So a write for these four is refused on a graphic, and reporting them there would put four values in front of you that writing the object back would be refused for. `noContextMenu` READS AS IT SOUNDS: true means the shortcut menu over a PDF is suppressed.

EVERY KIND REPORTS ITS CALCULATION-BACKED SETTINGS, and each of them carries the EXPRESSION the way FileMaker's calculation dialog shows it: `tooltip`, `hideCondition`, `accessibilityTitle` and `accessibilityHelp`, plus `placeholderText` and `entryCalculation` on a FIELD. A value a developer typed as plain text reads back QUOTED -- `"Hello there"` -- because that is what the file holds; a formula reads back unquoted. Each is ABSENT unless the object has one. `applyInFindMode` is the checkbox beside the hide condition and is reported ALWAYS on every kind, so it can be true with no `hideCondition` beside it -- which is a state FileMaker leaves behind when a condition is cleared in Pro, and it hides nothing. A TAB OR SLIDE PANEL REPORTS ITS CONTROL's `hideCondition` and `applyInFindMode`, because that is where FileMaker keeps them for a panel; the tooltip and the two accessibility strings are the panel's own.

`accessibilityLabel` IS ANOTHER OBJECT'S `id` -- the object whose text labels this one for a screen reader, which is Pro's "Click to select..." button in the Accessibility section. It is ABSENT both when the object has no label and when the stored reference names an object that is no longer on the layout, because reporting that would give you an `id` nothing resolves. Send 0 to clear one.

`scriptTriggers` ON AN OBJECT IS THAT OBJECT'S OWN, one entry per event, and it is a different set of events from the layout's `scriptTriggers` above -- OnObjectEnter, OnObjectExit, OnObjectModify, OnObjectSave, OnObjectKeystroke, OnObjectValidate, OnObjectAVPlayerChange, and OnPanelSwitch on a tab or slide control. Each entry names the `event`, the `script` it runs, the `modes` it fires in and its `parameter` if it has one, exactly as a layout trigger's does. THE KEY IS ABSENT ON A KIND THAT CANNOT HOLD A TRIGGER and `[]` on one that can and does not -- a label, a shape, a graphic, a button bar, a tab or slide PANEL and a group with no action report no key at all, and that is the same distinction `objects` draws between an empty container and a leaf. So the key appears exactly where a write for it is accepted, with one exception: a CHART reports its triggers and refuses every write, because this CLI cannot change a chart at all.

A BUTTON AND A POPOVER BUTTON REPORT THEIR ICON as `iconId`, `iconSize` and `iconPosition`, and a button bar SEGMENT reports them too -- a segment is a button. `iconId` is the image-library member the icon is stored as, the same kind of number `pictureId` is and in the same catalog, and it is ABSENT on a button with no icon. It is an identity rather than a write address: `icon` takes a FILE, and a file the library already holds is joined rather than stored twice. The other two are reported whatever the icon is, because the file stores them either way -- so `iconSize` on a button with no icon is the size an icon WOULD be drawn at, which is why a Pro-authored button with nothing showing still reports 16. AN ICON DRIVEN BY A CALCULATION IS NOT VISIBLE HERE: these three read normally on such a button, so what is reported can be an icon a formula overrides when it is drawn.

`showHandCursor` IS REPORTED WHEREVER FILEMAKER READS IT and absent everywhere else, so it appears exactly where a write for it is taken: on a BUTTON, a POPOVER BUTTON, a button bar SEGMENT, and on a GROUP once it carries an `action`. A group with no action reports no key, which is the same absent-versus-present distinction `scriptTriggers` draws and for the same reason -- a script step is what makes a group a button.

A PORTAL reports five of Pro's Portal Setup settings, always, and on nothing else: `initialRow`, `allowVerticalScrolling`, `scrollBarVisibility`, `allowDelete` and `resetScrollBarOnExit`. Each reads the way the dialog does, so `resetScrollBarOnExit` true means the scroll position is NOT retained -- the file stores the retaining bit and this is its negation. WATCH WHICH KEY IS WHICH CONTROL: `allowVerticalScrolling` is the checkbox and `scrollBarVisibility` (`always` or `whenScrolling`) is the picker beside it, which is the one the dialog labels "Show scroll bar:". The picker is reported even on a portal with no bar, where Pro greys it out, because the file stores it either way. `initialRow` is 1-BASED -- which row of the found set the portal starts at. THE DIALOG HOLDS MORE THAN THESE FIVE: its sort and its filter are backed by a stored sort order and a calculation and are reported nowhere yet, and its two row-styling checkboxes are styling. So these five do not describe a portal completely.

They are NOT the first entry of `objects`: a control's panels can be reordered without changing which one opens, so a control with three panels can report the second. A button bar carries `activeSegment` when a segment is marked as the current one, which FileMaker leaves unset on an ordinary bar. Each is absent when the object singles nothing out, and a slide control carries no `defaultPanel` because FileMaker stores none for one -- its default is its first panel, which `objects` already says.

An object carrying a NAMED THEME STYLE reports it under `style`, as the display name Pro's Inspector shows in its Style pop-up. Absent means the object wears its theme's default for its kind, which most objects do. The name is the theme's, not the object's: what the object stores is an internal id (`primary_button`, or `FM-38B338BC-...` for a style a developer made), and the theme holds the mapping. `update:layout`'s `style` takes the display name back, and "" removes the binding. ONE NAME CAN BE SEVERAL STYLES -- 'Transparent' is a different style for a button than for an edit box -- so the object's kind is what decides which one a write applies, and a name defined only for other kinds is refused with the list of what this object can wear.

A TURNED OBJECT reports `rotation` in whole degrees -- 90, 180 or 270. Absent means the object is upright, which is nearly all of them. IT DOES NOT AFFECT `bounds`: the rectangle reported is the stored one whatever the angle is, so a turned field reports the same rectangle it would have reported before it was turned. The file holds tenths of a degree internally, which is what a DDR export shows as 2700; the wire never uses them.

A POPOVER reports `popoverArrow`, which of its OWN edges carries the arrow pointing at its button -- so the popover opens on the OPPOSITE side: a popover reporting `left` sits to the RIGHT of its button. FileMaker's own vocabulary and its DDR export use the same words. It says which edge FileMaker will TRY FIRST when the popover opens, not where the popover will appear: the fallback goes through the other edges when the first does not fit the screen, and in Layout mode the popover keeps whatever rectangle `bounds` reports.

A POPOVER also reports `showTitleBar`, always, and it reads the way Pro's checkbox does: false means the strip along the top of the popover is not drawn. The file stores the opposite bit, `kHideTitleBar`, so a DDR export's raw flag number is the negation of this. A popover whose bar is hidden STILL REPORTS ITS `title`, because the title is stored separately and comes back when the bar does.

A BUTTON BAR reports `orientation`, `horizontal` or `vertical`, always and on nothing else. A SEGMENT does not report it: which way the bar runs is what decides where each segment sits, so it belongs to the bar a segment is nested under. `update:layout` takes the word back and turning the bar moves every segment while leaving the bar's own `bounds` alone.

A GROUP reports `action`, the same step object a button does and always, because FileMaker turns a group into a button by giving it a script step -- that is what Pro's Button Setup dialog does to a selection. A group with no action reports `{"stepID": 0}`, FileMaker's own "Do Nothing", and is an ordinary group rather than a broken button.

A SLIDE CONTROL reports `showNavigationDots` and `enableSwipeGestures`, which are the two checkboxes in Pro's Slide Control Setup dialog. Both are always reported on a slide control and on nothing else. THEY READ THE WAY PRO'S CHECKBOXES DO: `showNavigationDots` false means the dots are hidden. The file stores the opposite two bits, so a DDR export's raw `slideFlagSet` number is the negation of these; `update:layout` takes the same two words back in the same sense. Neither affects the control's panels or its rectangle -- hiding the dots does not reclaim the space they occupied, which is the style's to give.

A TAB CONTROL reports `tabWidthStyle`, `tabWidthModifier`, `tabWidthUnits` and `tabsShareSingleStyle` -- the stored parts of Pro's Tab Control Setup dialog, on the control and not on its panels. `tabWidthModifier` IS IN POINTS whatever `tabWidthUnits` says; the unit is only what Pro's dialog displays, and it is the one of the four that can be absent, because the stored field can hold a value naming no unit. The modifier is used by three of the five width styles and is reported for all of them. THE TAB POSITION AND THE TAB HEIGHT ARE NOT REPORTED, deliberately: nothing in FileMaker reads the position and the height is recomputed from the font on every layout pass, so neither is a setting a caller could act on.

A FIELD reports Pro's Inspector Behavior section: `browseEntry` and `findEntry`, then `selectContentsOnEntry`, `exitOnTab`, `exitOnReturn`, `exitOnEnter`, `applyVisualSpellChecking`, `quickFind`, `inputMode` and `keyboardType`. The first eight are always present on a field; `inputMode` and `keyboardType` are absent only when the stored byte holds a value naming none of their options, which FileMaker itself cannot author. THE ENTRY VALUES ARE PRO'S PICKER WORDS -- `edit`, `selectOnly`, `viewOnly` and `setByCalculation` -- and a field reading `setByCalculation` is entered or not according to its `entryCalculation`, which is reported beside them. `applyVisualSpellChecking` and `quickFind` READ POSITIVELY: true means misspellings are underlined and the field is searched, which is the opposite sense from the bits the file stores. A LABEL REPORTS `quickFind` TOO, and only where FileMaker would offer it: a label's Quick Find searches the FIELDS its merge fields reference, so the key appears on a label carrying at least one merge field that names a searchable field and is absent on every other label. Absent rather than false, because the engine ignores the stored value on a label it will not search, so a reported false would be a value the write then refuses.

A FIELD also reports the rest of Pro's Data section, always: `repetitionCount` and `repetitionOrientation`, `allowEntryOfOtherValues`, `allowEditingOfValueList`, `includeShowHideIcon`, `autoComplete`, `showVerticalScrollBar`, `scrollBarVisibility`, `showPlaceholderInFindMode` and `overrideDataFormattingWithValueList` -- alongside `control` and `valueList`, which are that section's first two controls. EVERY ONE IS REPORTED WHATEVER THE CONTROL STYLE, because the file stores each either way and a caller reproducing a field needs all of them; `allowEditingOfValueList` on an edit box is stored and inert rather than absent. `repetitionCount` IS THE COUNT WITHOUT ITS SIGN -- the file keeps one signed number whose sign is the orientation, and reporting it raw would hide a layout choice inside a quantity. `includeShowHideIcon` is the checkbox a developer ticks; whether a pop-up menu actually draws the icon also depends on a compatibility bit this CLI sets for you when you write the key.

A FIELD AND A GRAPHIC BOTH REPORT how the picture inside them is fitted, which is the Graphic tab of Pro's Data Formatting section: `graphicSizing` (`cropToFrame`, `reduceToFit`, `enlargeToFit` or `reduceOrEnlargeToFit`), `maintainOriginalProportions`, `horizontalAlignment` (`left`, `center` or `right`) and `verticalAlignment` (`top`, `center` or `bottom`). All four always, on both kinds. WHAT MADE THE OBJECT SHOWS UP HERE: a field this CLI created reports `cropToFrame` with proportions false, one FileMaker Pro created reports `reduceToFit` with proportions TRUE, and a GRAPHIC this CLI created reports `reduceOrEnlargeToFit` with proportions FALSE -- so its picture is stretched to fill the object until you set `maintainOriginalProportions`. An alignment is ABSENT only for a stored value naming no choice, which FileMaker's own pickers cannot produce.

A FIELD ALSO REPORTS THE FOUR SETTINGS FOR INTERACTIVE CONTENT, and a graphic does not: `optimizeFor` (`images` or `interactiveContent`), `autoPlay`, `noContextMenu` and `preservePdfTransparency`. They are the rest of the same Graphic tab and they are what makes a container field show a PDF, an audio file or a video rather than a still picture. A GRAPHIC REPORTS NONE OF THEM even though it has somewhere to keep them, because nothing in FileMaker reads them on one -- a graphic's transparency is preserved regardless of what is stored. So a write for these four is refused on a graphic, and reporting them there would put four values in front of you that writing the object back would be refused for. `noContextMenu` READS AS IT SOUNDS: true means the shortcut menu over a PDF is suppressed.

EVERY KIND REPORTS ITS CALCULATION-BACKED SETTINGS, and each of them carries the EXPRESSION the way FileMaker's calculation dialog shows it: `tooltip`, `hideCondition`, `accessibilityTitle` and `accessibilityHelp`, plus `placeholderText` and `entryCalculation` on a FIELD. A value a developer typed as plain text reads back QUOTED -- `"Hello there"` -- because that is what the file holds; a formula reads back unquoted. Each is ABSENT unless the object has one. `applyInFindMode` is the checkbox beside the hide condition and is reported ALWAYS on every kind, so it can be true with no `hideCondition` beside it -- which is a state FileMaker leaves behind when a condition is cleared in Pro, and it hides nothing. A TAB OR SLIDE PANEL REPORTS ITS CONTROL's `hideCondition` and `applyInFindMode`, because that is where FileMaker keeps them for a panel; the tooltip and the two accessibility strings are the panel's own.

`accessibilityLabel` IS ANOTHER OBJECT'S `id` -- the object whose text labels this one for a screen reader, which is Pro's "Click to select..." button in the Accessibility section. It is ABSENT both when the object has no label and when the stored reference names an object that is no longer on the layout, because reporting that would give you an `id` nothing resolves. Send 0 to clear one.

`scriptTriggers` ON AN OBJECT IS THAT OBJECT'S OWN, one entry per event, and it is a different set of events from the layout's `scriptTriggers` above -- OnObjectEnter, OnObjectExit, OnObjectModify, OnObjectSave, OnObjectKeystroke, OnObjectValidate, OnObjectAVPlayerChange, and OnPanelSwitch on a tab or slide control. Each entry names the `event`, the `script` it runs, the `modes` it fires in and its `parameter` if it has one, exactly as a layout trigger's does. THE KEY IS ABSENT ON A KIND THAT CANNOT HOLD A TRIGGER and `[]` on one that can and does not -- a label, a shape, a graphic, a button bar, a tab or slide PANEL and a group with no action report no key at all, and that is the same distinction `objects` draws between an empty container and a leaf. So the key appears exactly where a write for it is accepted, with one exception: a CHART reports its triggers and refuses every write, because this CLI cannot change a chart at all.

A BUTTON AND A POPOVER BUTTON REPORT THEIR ICON as `iconId`, `iconSize` and `iconPosition`, and a button bar SEGMENT reports them too -- a segment is a button. `iconId` is the image-library member the icon is stored as, the same kind of number `pictureId` is and in the same catalog, and it is ABSENT on a button with no icon. It is an identity rather than a write address: `icon` takes a FILE, and a file the library already holds is joined rather than stored twice. The other two are reported whatever the icon is, because the file stores them either way -- so `iconSize` on a button with no icon is the size an icon WOULD be drawn at, which is why a Pro-authored button with nothing showing still reports 16. AN ICON DRIVEN BY A CALCULATION IS NOT VISIBLE HERE: these three read normally on such a button, so what is reported can be an icon a formula overrides when it is drawn.

`showHandCursor` IS REPORTED WHEREVER FILEMAKER READS IT and absent everywhere else, so it appears exactly where a write for it is taken: on a BUTTON, a POPOVER BUTTON, a button bar SEGMENT, and on a GROUP once it carries an `action`. A group with no action reports no key, which is the same absent-versus-present distinction `scriptTriggers` draws and for the same reason -- a script step is what makes a group a button.

A PORTAL reports five of Pro's Portal Setup settings, always, and on nothing else: `initialRow`, `allowVerticalScrolling`, `scrollBarVisibility`, `allowDelete` and `resetScrollBarOnExit`. Each reads the way the dialog does, so `resetScrollBarOnExit` true means the scroll position is NOT retained -- the file stores the retaining bit and this is its negation. WATCH WHICH KEY IS WHICH CONTROL: `allowVerticalScrolling` is the checkbox and `scrollBarVisibility` (`always` or `whenScrolling`) is the picker beside it, which is the one the dialog labels "Show scroll bar:". The picker is reported even on a portal with no bar, where Pro greys it out, because the file stores it either way. `initialRow` is 1-BASED -- which row of the found set the portal starts at. THE DIALOG HOLDS MORE THAN THESE FIVE: its sort and its filter are backed by a stored sort order and a calculation and are reported nowhere yet, and its two row-styling checkboxes are styling. So these five do not describe a portal completely.
