nodes.title: read:valueList
nodes.summary: Lists every value list, or describes one by name or id
notes: FileMaker offers three orderings for a value list catalog; this CLI always sorts by id ascending, so the order is this CLI's contract rather than FileMaker's default.

`detail` reports each listed value list exactly as a describe of it would -- its type, its values, its field specs and its options -- so one call answers for the whole catalog what would otherwise take one call per list. Omitted, an item is `{name,id}`, which is what a listing has always reported.

`filter` NARROWS a listing and does nothing else. Every value list that comes back is reported in exactly the shape an unfiltered listing gives it, so a filter changes which members appear and never what any one of them says.
`total` is how many value lists the file has, unfiltered; `returned` counts the ones that came back. A filtered listing therefore reports both what matched and what it was matched against.

Matching ignores case, and `name` is a pattern: `*` stands for any run of characters and `?` for exactly one, so `status*` and `*_archive` both work. There is no escape, so a list whose name really contains `*` or `?` cannot be matched literally.

A filter matching nothing is `ok` with `"items":[]` and `returned` of 0 -- a filter is a test each member is put to rather than an address, so a pattern nothing matches is not `not_found`. A misspelled pattern therefore looks exactly like an empty catalog.

`name` filters an UNDETAILED listing, which is `{name,id}` and nothing else. `type` and `startTable` filter the DETAILED item instead, so either is refused with `invalid_field` unless the same op also sends `detail`:true -- naming the kind of list a caller wants is the reason `detail` exists to be asked for.
A describe reports the DEFINITION, never an evaluation: a field-based list is not resolved against records, because records are out of this tool's scope.

Only the keys meaningful for the CURRENT `type` are emitted. FileMaker does not clear a departed type's attributes -- measured 2026-07-26, the old field specs and option bits are still stored and readable -- so reporting them would describe a list that does not behave that way.
`shadow` and `supportsAutoComplete` are read-only and engine-derived, and are always present. `options` is always all three booleans, never a partial object.

`sortLanguage` is the one field-list key reported CONDITIONALLY: it appears only when a list overrides its collation. Absent means the sorting field's own language, so a read feeds back into a create unchanged rather than turning FileMaker's default into a choice.

An unknown `name`/`id` is `not_found` with closest-name suggestions -- the GENERIC code, as `read:table` uses, while the write verbs below use `valueList_not_found`. That split matches the existing table/field ops rather than introducing a new convention.

nodes.title: update:valueList
nodes.summary: Renames a value list, edits its attributes, or switches its type
semanticChecks: On a switch to type 'field', 'showRelatedOnly' requires 'startTable' -- re-checked on a switch only, because 'showRelatedOnly' with no 'startTable' in a partial edit may be legitimate against a list that already has one.
On a switch to type 'field', 'sortBySecondField' requires 'secondField'.
On a switch to type 'field', 'showSecondFieldOnly' requires 'secondField'.
A custom value must not contain a carriage return: FileMaker separates the values of a custom list with CR, so it would be read back as two values.

'secondField' must name a different field than 'field', and (via a separate check against the join graph) an occurrence related to 'field''s or the same one -- unlike the three rules above, both apply whenever 'field' and 'secondField' are BOTH sent together, whether switching to type 'field' or plainly editing both, because neither depends on what the list's type turns out to be.
An 'options' object with NO member set does not count as a change, so it does not satisfy the at-least-one-change rule on its own.
A malformed 'calculation' is refused with 'invalid_field' carrying FileMaker's own parse error, and the list is left unchanged.
notes: A type switch also CLEARS the attributes of the type being left. FileMaker does not: measured, a list switched from `field` to `custom` still has its old field specs and option bits stored and readable. The CLI zeroes them on write AND omits them on read -- belt and braces, because the write-side clear cannot reach a list FileMaker itself created.

A partial edit (no `type`) that touches a key belonging to the list's CURRENT type's opposite is `invalid_field`, with a message saying to switch the type explicitly -- and this also fires against a list left as `external`, or against `calculation`'s own key sent to a list of a different type, naming that actual type rather than assuming a binary custom/field split.
A case-only rename of the same list is allowed; `newName` naming a DIFFERENT list, compared case-insensitively, is `valueList_exists`.
`result` is `{name,id}` with the list's id unchanged.
